13-1071.00:18861.short: Explain HR policies, CAO rules, procedures and Dutch law to managers and employees.

steps.what: Receive policy question from manager or employee
Find the right policy page, CAO article or law text

loop.input: question plus indexed policies, both CAOs and selected law texts
loop.output: ranked list of clauses with document version
loop.check: only documents from the approved SharePoint library and wetten.overheid.nl are indexed
loop.stop: top five clauses; none above threshold means escalate
loop.why_not_simpler: keyword search fails on everyday wording like 'snipperdag' versus 'verlof'

steps.what: Write explanation in plain Dutch or English

loop.output: short answer with clause citations and an AI disclosure line
loop.check: every sentence must map to a cited clause; questions naming a person, absence, dismissal or pay dispute are never answered and go to the HRBP
loop.stop: one answer; if the check fails, a ticket to the HRBP with the draft attached
loop.why_not_simpler: answers must be phrased for the asker's situation, which a static FAQ cannot do

steps.what: Handle follow-ups, edge cases and personal situations
Fix unclear or missing policy text

13-1071.00:18861.design: An answer desk in Teams built on the M365 tenant retrieves from one approved SharePoint library (policies, both CAOs, poortwachter procedure) and answers general questions with citations and an AI disclosure; anything personal becomes a ticket for the site HRBP. A weekly report of unanswered and escalated questions feeds policy fixes.
13-1071.00:18861.previous_blocker: Earlier bots needed hand-built intent trees and failed on Dutch everyday wording and CAO detail.
13-1071.00:18861.enabler_now: Retrieval with a model that cites clauses, on content HR already owns, is now standard in M365 and similar tools.
13-1071.00:18861.still_hard: Keeping the source library current and versioned, and a wrong answer on law (ontslag, verzuim) has legal cost; the escalation line must be strict.
13-1071.00:18861.human_edge: Knowing when a 'general' question is really about one person, and explaining a hard rule so it is accepted.

ambition.what: Every new team leader gets a policy answer within minutes for every question, instead of saving them up for the monthly HRBP meeting.

13-1071.00:18861.altitude: The HRBP stops answering the same leave and overtime questions and owns the escalated cases and the quality of the policy library.

reach.task: Onboarding new team leaders
reach.learn: The top 20 questions new leaders ask, to build them into onboarding.

reach.task: Approving policy changes
reach.learn: Which policies generate most confusion, measured, not guessed.

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina runs an HR policy agent with ticket fallback, CSAT 4.1.
IBM Ask HR saved about 40% with HRBPs as second line.
Average time saved by HR staff using chatbots was about 3%.
AI disclosure is required for systems interacting with people.

assumptions: Policies live in one SharePoint library that HR controls.
Questions in Dutch and English, some Polish speakers among warehouse staff.
unknowns: How many policy questions per week reach the three HRBPs today.
Whether the policies and CAO summaries are up to date.
Languages needed for flex workers.
research_questions: In a two-week test on 200 real past questions, what share does the desk answer correctly with citations?
How often does a 'general' question turn out to be personal, and does the filter catch it?
Do managers keep using the desk after week four?

13-1071.00:18859.short: Process new-hire paperwork: collect data, enter employee and contract in AFAS, issue contract, notify others.

steps.what: Collect new-hire personal data, bank details, tax form, ID copy
Re-key offer and personal data into AFAS employee and contract
Draft the employment contract from the Word template per CAO
Send the contract for signature and chase it
Check the original ID document in person on day one
Notify payroll, IT, manager; enrol in Studytube mandatory courses

13-1071.00:18859.design: A hire in Recruitee triggers a scheduled integration that creates a draft employee and contract in AFAS for the administrator to approve. AFAS Pocket onboarding collects the new hire's own data and documents, with Jonas reading the documents into fields. After approval, AFAS generates the CAO contract from a template and sends it for signature, and the same job notifies payroll, IT and the manager and enrols the hire in Studytube by role.
13-1071.00:18859.previous_blocker: Recruitee and AFAS were never linked. Contract variants per CAO and site lived in Word templates, and nobody owned building the connector.
13-1071.00:18859.enabler_now: AFAS Profit 8 has Pocket pre-boarding and Jonas document reading [S4]. Connector code between documented APIs is now cheap to write and test.
13-1071.00:18859.still_hard: Contract variants for two CAOs, three sites and fixed-term rules need careful templating. The employer must still check original ID documents in person.
13-1071.00:18859.human_edge: Approving the contract terms, handling unusual offers, and checking the ID face to face stay with the administrator.

ambition.what: Check every new hire's dossier for completeness before day one, not after the first payroll run.

13-1071.00:18859.altitude: The administrator approves drafts and handles exceptions instead of typing. They decide whether a dossier is ready for the payroll cut-off.

reach.task: Make offers in Recruitee
reach.learn: Which offer fields AFAS needs, so offers arrive complete and the integration does not stop

reach.task: Add new hires to the month-close payroll run
reach.learn: Payroll cut-off dates and loonheffing rules, so drafts are approved in time

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 Jonas reads documents into dossier fields and Pocket lets new hires submit data before day one
SixFifty drafts contracts and sends them for signature within strict workflows on a maintained law base (US only)
Recruitee and AFAS both expose APIs for candidate and employee records

assumptions: Roughly 300 to 500 hires a year including warehouse staff, not counting agency flex workers
AFAS Profit is or can be upgraded to version 8
Contract templates are stable enough to move into AFAS

Whether the AFAS licence includes Pocket onboarding and Jonas
How many contract template variants exist
Which e-signature method is already used
research_questions: How many contract variants are really in use, and can they be built as AFAS templates with conditional clauses?
What is Jonas's field error rate on Dutch ID copies and loonheffing forms in a two-week test?
How often do Recruitee offers lack fields AFAS requires, and who should fix them?
Does a direct Recruitee-to-AFAS draft cut the days from offer accepted to complete dossier?

13-1071.00:18866.short: Process hires, exits, leave, transfers and promotions in AFAS, with contract letters and notifications.

steps.what: Receive event request from Recruitee, HRBP or manager
Check CAO scale, contract chain, notice period and approvals
Enter contract, function, salary and cost centre change in AFAS
Draft contract or letter from SharePoint template and send for signature
Notify payroll, IT, site lead and L&D of the change

13-1071.00:18866.design: A Recruitee-to-AFAS connector and an AFAS manager form start every personnel action as one AFAS workflow. Deterministic checks (CAO scale, ketenregeling, notice period, approvals present) run in code, the change is prepared in AFAS for one-click approval, the contract is merged from the SharePoint template, and notifications and Studytube enrolments go out automatically.
13-1071.00:18866.previous_blocker: Recruitee, AFAS, SharePoint templates and Studytube were never connected, and CAO rules lived in people's heads and PDFs.
13-1071.00:18866.enabler_now: Both Recruitee and AFAS have APIs and AI coding makes connectors and rule code cheap; the CAO rules can be written down once and tested.
13-1071.00:18866.still_hard: Writing the CAO and warehouse-CAO rules completely, including exceptions; keeping templates current with CAO changes; non-standard deals agreed by managers.
13-1071.00:18866.human_edge: Spotting deals that do not fit the rules and agreeing them with the HRBP; approving changes that affect pay and contract status.

13-1071.00:18866.altitude: The administrator approves prepared changes and handles rule breaks instead of typing. They own the CAO rule table with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist.

reach.task: Maintaining salary scales and CAO changes
reach.learn: How scale rules are encoded, so a CAO update changes one table, not templates by hand.

reach.task: Making offers in Recruitee
reach.learn: Which offer fields AFAS needs, so offers are complete at the source.

Dutch contract chain rules and CAO scales are fixed rules that code can check.

Contract templates on SharePoint are few enough to merge from structured fields.
unknowns: Number of personnel actions per month by type.
Whether an e-signature tool is in use.
How often managers agree terms outside the CAO.

Can 90% of contracts be generated from fields without free-text edits?
Does the Recruitee-AFAS connector create a complete employee record without manual fixes in a test of 20 hires?

13-1071.00:18868.short: Read applications in Recruitee against the vacancy and decide who fits the job requirements.

steps.what: Take the job order from the hiring manager and set requirements
Open each application and read CV and motivation

loop.input: CV and application form text from Recruitee
loop.output: structured candidate facts (licences, code 95, forklift/VCA certificates, years in role, shift availability, location) each with a quoted source line
loop.check: Every fact must quote a line found in the CV; facts without a quote are dropped; recruiter sees facts next to the CV
loop.stop: One pass per CV, one retry on schema error, then mark 'read manually'
loop.why_not_simpler: CVs are free text in many layouts and languages; fixed parsing misses most facts.

steps.what: Check must-haves: work permit, licences, certificates, shifts, travel distance
Judge overall fit and move candidate to a pipeline stage
Write screening notes in the candidate record

13-1071.00:18868.design: Configure a structured intake form in Recruitee so each vacancy has explicit must-haves and nice-to-haves. A small job on the governed HR platform pulls new applications through the Recruitee API, extracts quoted facts with a bounded model step, runs the must-have rules and writes a fact panel and a draft screening note back into Recruitee. The recruiter makes every stage move; nothing rejects automatically and there is no single match score.
13-1071.00:18868.previous_blocker: CVs are unstructured and vary wildly; rule-based parsers were too weak and full matching tools raised legal and works-council concerns.
13-1071.00:18868.enabler_now: Models can extract facts with quoted evidence reliably enough to review, and AI coding makes the Recruitee integration and rules a days-long build.
13-1071.00:18868.still_hard: Deciding fit for people with unusual paths, and keeping extraction errors from silently excluding candidates. Works council consent and, from 2 December 2027, high-risk AI Act duties apply.
13-1071.00:18868.human_edge: Seeing potential in an unusual CV and knowing what a site manager really needs beyond the written requirements.

ambition.what: Every applicant gets a must-have check within one working day of applying, instead of when the recruiter gets to the pile.

13-1071.00:18868.altitude: The recruiter spends less time reading and more time on intake with managers; they gain the right to sharpen must-haves per vacancy with data on why candidates fail them.

reach.task: Report on days per pipeline stage and drop-off reasons
reach.learn: Use the structured must-have data to show which requirements shrink the pool most.

reach.task: Track mandatory certificates (forklift, VCA) in Studytube
reach.learn: Hires missing a certificate can be routed to training before day one.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 builds a profile from an application and calculates a match score against vacancies.
67% of hiring leaders use AI for CV screening; 26% fear they no longer see some candidates.
No rejection may be based solely on an automated score; review must be meaningful.
CV screening tools almost always need prior works council consent.
Filtering applications becomes high-risk under the AI Act from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Recruitee API access is available on the current plan.
Most warehouse and driver vacancies have clear must-haves (licence, certificates, shifts).
unknowns: Applications per vacancy and per month by site.
Whether the OR already has a regulation on HR software.
Whether Noordhaven uses or plans AFAS Profit 8 recruitment features.
research_questions: How many applications per month fail on a must-have, and how long does reading them take today?
On 200 past CVs, how often does extraction miss or invent a licence or certificate?
Will the works council consent to fact extraction without ranking?
Does Recruitee's own screening or questions cover the must-haves without custom code?

loop.output: draft answer citing the source paragraph
loop.check: Answer must cite a source passage; pay figures must match the CAO table lookup exactly; recruiter edits and sends
loop.stop: One draft per question; if no source matches, show 'no answer in sources' and the recruiter answers

Write vacancy text and candidate information

loop.output: vacancy text and one-page info pack in Dutch and English
loop.check: Pay, hours and allowances are inserted from the lookup, not written by the model; recruiter approves before publishing
loop.stop: Two drafts at most, then recruiter writes
loop.why_not_simpler: Readable job text needs prose; the facts themselves come from templates and tables.

steps.what: Explain offer terms and answer doubts in a call

A generator turns it into a vacancy text and a per-vacancy info pack linked from every Recruitee vacancy and invitation mail. An internal answer desk drafts cited replies to remaining candidate mails for the recruiter to send.
13-1071.00:18860.previous_blocker: Pay and shift facts live in the CAO PDF, AFAS and people's heads, so each answer needed a lookup and a fresh mail.
13-1071.00:18860.enabler_now: Cheap generation of documents from structured tables and cited retrieval over policy text, both quick to build with AI coding.
13-1071.00:18860.still_hard: Keeping the fact table current after CAO changes and indexation; any wrong pay figure has legal and trust costs.
13-1071.00:18860.human_edge: Reading a candidate's doubts in a call and being honest about night shifts, peak season and physical work.

ambition.what: A one-page info pack per vacancy (pay scale, shifts, travel allowance, site, first week) sent with every interview invite.

13-1071.00:18860.altitude: Fewer repeat phone calls; the recruiter spends calls on doubts, not facts, and decides when info packs are good enough to publish.

reach.task: Maintain CAO pay scales and allowances
reach.learn: Own the fact table that feeds candidate information so pay quoted to candidates matches payroll.

reach.task: Prepare employment contracts in AFAS

evidence.claim: 57% of hiring leaders use AI for job descriptions.
Recruiter-reviewed emails and job ads need no AI label; a candidate-facing chatbot must say it is AI.
Cited retrieval over policy documents can draft answers for review.

No candidate-facing chatbot is built, so no AI notice is needed.
unknowns: Share of candidate contacts that are fact questions versus doubts.
Languages candidates use, especially for warehouse roles.
Who keeps CAO and site facts current today.

13-1071.00:18871.short: Shortlist qualified candidates, screen them and recommend hires to hiring managers.

Phone screen or interview shortlisted candidates
Write candidate profile and recommendation for the hiring manager

loop.input: recruiter's own scorecard and notes plus candidate facts (no interview recordings)
loop.output: one-page profile per candidate with strengths, gaps and the recruiter's recommendation
loop.check: Every statement must trace to a scorecard field or note; recruiter edits and signs off; no score or ranking added by the model

steps.what: Chase manager feedback and interview slots
Discuss recommendation with hiring manager and agree next step

A scheduled job reads Recruitee stage dates and nudges managers in Teams when feedback is overdue, with a weekly list of candidates stuck too long. 13-1071.00:18871.previous_blocker: Notes were scattered across mail and Word, and nudging managers took a person watching every pipeline.
13-1071.00:18871.enabler_now: Stage dates are available through the Recruitee API, and profiles can be drafted from structured scorecards in seconds.
13-1071.00:18871.still_hard: Getting managers to act on nudges and to read the profile rather than replace the interview; bias in the recommendation itself.
13-1071.00:18871.human_edge: Judging motivation, reliability and team fit in conversation and standing behind a recommendation to a site manager.

reach.learn: Use stage-delay data per manager to coach on decision speed.

reach.task: Measure 90-day retention by hire
reach.learn: Link recommendations and scorecards to 90-day outcomes to test what predicts success.

Interview summaries become the record; notetakers err and store unlawful questions.
Evaluating candidates is high-risk under the AI Act from 2 December 2027.
The employer stays liable for discrimination by hiring tools.

Managers use Teams daily.
unknowns: Average days from shortlist to manager decision today.
Whether managers have Recruitee accounts or work by mail.
Works council view on tracking manager response times.
research_questions: How many days does a shortlisted candidate wait for manager feedback today, per site?
Do Teams nudges shorten that wait in a four-week pilot on one site?
Do managers find generated profiles as useful as recruiter-written ones?

13-1071.00:18863.short: Keep org charts, the employee handbook, directories and evaluation forms current after changes in AFAS, the CAO or policy.

steps.what: Notice a change from manager mail, AFAS mutation or CAO update
Update org charts and staff directories by hand
Edit handbook and policy text after CAO or policy changes

loop.input: new CAO text or policy decision and the affected handbook sections
loop.output: tracked-changes redline with a list of sections touched
loop.check: the administrator and HRBP review every change; section list is compared with a keyword search across the handbook for missed hits
loop.stop: one draft per change; sections the model is unsure of are flagged, not changed
loop.why_not_simpler: CAO changes are written as legal prose; finding and rewording every affected handbook section needs reading free text.

steps.what: Adjust performance evaluation forms and templates
Publish new versions on SharePoint and inform staff

13-1071.00:18863.design: Org charts and directories are generated each night from the AFAS org structure, either in Power BI or through the Microsoft 365 directory, so they are no longer kept by hand. Handbook changes run as a SharePoint approval flow: a bounded model step drafts a redline from the CAO or policy change, the HRBP approves it, and publishing and the Teams notice are automatic.
13-1071.00:18863.previous_blocker: Org data in AFAS was not trusted enough to publish directly, and handbook updates needed someone to read the CAO and find every affected section.
13-1071.00:18863.enabler_now: AFAS can feed the M365 directory and Power BI, and models can draft redlines from legal text with a person checking them.
13-1071.00:18863.still_hard: AFAS data quality (managers, cost centres, flex workers who are not in AFAS) sets the quality of the generated org charts. Handbook wording that has legal effect still needs an HRBP and sometimes OR consent under WOR art. 27.
13-1071.00:18863.human_edge: Judging how a CAO change applies to Noordhaven's own warehouse arrangements, and writing policy text that shift workers on the floor understand.

ambition.what: A handbook Q&A in Teams for all 1,200 staff, labelled as AI and answering from the maintained handbook, with a ticket to HR when it cannot answer.

13-1071.00:18863.altitude: The administrator becomes the handbook content owner instead of the person who copy-edits charts. They decide the structure of the handbook and flag which changes need the HRBP or the OR.

reach.task: Translating CAO and policy changes into local arrangements
reach.learn: Which handbook clauses are CAO-bound and which are company policy, so redlines go to the right approver.

How many handbook sections changed after the last CAO round, and how long did the update take?

13-1071.00:18857.short: Tell applicants where their application stands, by mail and by phone, including rejections.

13-1071.00:18857.still_hard: Writing rejection templates that are kind and specific enough, and keeping stage data accurate so the right mail goes out.
13-1071.00:18857.human_edge: Delivering a rejection after an interview in a way that keeps the candidate willing to apply again or recommend Noordhaven.

13-1071.00:18857.altitude: The recruiter no longer hunts for who is owed an update; they decide the contact standard per stage and spend the time on post-interview calls.

reach.learn: Reuse the stage-triggered mail pattern for pre-boarding messages.

reach.task: Report on candidate experience and drop-off
